sujood.title: Pour your heart out in sujūd
sujood.do: Pray two rakʿahs, or your next prayer, and make a lot of du’a in prostration. Tell Allah everything that is on your heart.
sujood.en: The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so make abundant du’a.
sujood.quote_by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

istighfar.title: Ask forgiveness: istighfār
istighfar.do: Say it slowly, with your heart present. The Prophet ﷺ said he did this more than seventy times a day. No fixed number is required of you, so the counter is just a help.
istighfar.en: I seek forgiveness from Allah and turn to Him in repentance.
istighfar.quote_by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
istighfar.quote: By Allah, I seek forgiveness from Allah and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day.

tasbih100.title: SubḥānAllāhi wa bi-ḥamdih
tasbih100.do: Say it a hundred times, for example after Fajr or before bed.
tasbih100.en: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him.
tasbih100.quote: Whoever says “SubḥānAllāhi wa bi-ḥamdih” one hundred times a day, his sins will be forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea.
tasbih100.quote_by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

lahawla.title: Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh
lahawla.do: Say it whenever you feel you don’t have the strength. It means admitting that your strength comes from Allah.
lahawla.ar: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
lahawla.tr: Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh.
lahawla.en: There is no power and no strength except with Allah.
lahawla.quote: Shall I not tell you of a treasure from the treasures of Paradise? It is: lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh.
lahawla.quote_by: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him)

counters.label: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ

dhikr.title: Remember Allah with the four beloved phrases
dhikr.do: Breathe slowly and say any of these quietly, as many times as feels right. There is no fixed number, so the counters are only a help.
dhikr.ar: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
dhikr.tr: SubḥānAllāh, wal-ḥamdu lillāh, wa lā ilāha illallāh, wallāhu akbar.
dhikr.en: Glory be to Allah; praise be to Allah; there is no god but Allah; Allah is the Greatest.
dhikr.quote: The most beloved words to Allah are four: SubḥānAllāh, Alḥamdulillāh, Lā ilāha illallāh and Allāhu akbar. It does not matter which one you begin with.
dhikr.quote_by: Samurah ibn Jundub (may Allah be pleased with him)
dhikr.extra: Also: “Truly, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find peace” (13:28), and the Prophet ﷺ said the one who remembers his Lord and the one who does not are like the living and the dead (Bukhari 6407).

quran.title: Read a few verses slowly
quran.do: Open the Qur’an, read a short passage with a translation, and let it be a conversation. Even five verses count.
quran.en: O mankind, there has come to you instruction from your Lord and healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers.
quran.quote: Recite the Qur’an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who recite it.
quran.quote_by: Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī (may Allah be pleased with him)

salawat.title: Send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ
salawat.do: Say “ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam” or the fuller ṣalawāt of the prayer. It is also a way to feel close to him.
salawat.en: Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, ask [Allah to confer] blessing upon him and ask [Allah to grant him] peace.
salawat.quote: Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah will send blessings upon him ten times.
salawat.quote_by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
salawat.extra: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb (may Allah be pleased with him) asked the Prophet ﷺ how much of his du’a he should devote to sending blessings on him. When Ubayy offered all of it, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Then your worries will be taken care of and your sins forgiven” (Tirmidhī 2457, graded ḥasan).

quls.title: The three Quls, morning and evening
quls.do: Recite Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, al-Falaq and an-Nās, three times each, in the morning and in the evening.
quls.en: Say, “He is Allah, [who is] One, Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent.” Say, “I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak, from the evil of that which He created, and from the evil of darkness when it settles, and from the evil of the blowers in knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies.” Say, “I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the Sovereign of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer – who whispers [evil] into the breasts of mankind – among jinn and among mankind.”
quls.quote: Recite “Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad” and the two Muʿawwidhatayn three times in the morning and in the evening; they will suffice you against everything.
quls.quote_by: ʿAbdullāh ibn Khubayb (may Allah be pleased with him)

kindness.title: Do one small kindness today
kindness.do: Send a kind message, smile, check on someone, or help with something small. Doing good for others often lifts the heart.
kindness.quote: Do not belittle any good deed, even if it is meeting your brother with a cheerful face.
kindness.quote_by: Abū Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him)
kindness.extra: And: Allah helps His servant as long as the servant is helping his brother (Muslim 2699).

shukr.title: Name three blessings and say Alḥamdulillāh
shukr.do: Before you move on, say out loud three specific things you have. Gratitude changes where your attention sits.
shukr.quote_by: Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him)
shukr.extra: Allah says: “If you are grateful, I will surely increase you” (14:7).

tasbih_sleep.title: The bedtime tasbīḥ
tasbih_sleep.do: When you lie down, say SubḥānAllāh 33 times, Alḥamdulillāh 33 times and Allāhu akbar 34 times.
tasbih_sleep.quote: When you go to your bed, say SubḥānAllāh thirty-three times, Alḥamdulillāh thirty-three times and Allāhu akbar thirty-four times; that is better for you than a servant.
tasbih_sleep.quote_by: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him)

ayatkursi.title: Ayat al-Kursī before sleep
ayatkursi.do: Read Ayat al-Kursī when you go to bed.
ayatkursi.en: Allah – there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursī extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.
ayatkursi.quote: When you go to your bed, recite Āyat al-Kursī; a guardian from Allah will stay with you and Satan will not come near you until morning.
ayatkursi.quote_by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

hands.title: Raise your hands and ask
hands.do: Raise your hands and ask Allah for what you need, in your own words. A single sentence is enough.
hands.quote: Your Lord is Ever-Living and Generous. He is shy to turn away empty the hands of His servant when he raises them to Him.
hands.quote_by: Salmān al-Fārisī (may Allah be pleased with him)

rizq.title: Istighfār for provision
rizq.do: Make istighfār part of your daily routine. Nūḥ ﷺ told his people that seeking forgiveness is connected with Allah’s bounty.
rizq.en: And I said, “Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in [continuing] showers and will give you increase in wealth and children and provide for you gardens and provide for you rivers.”
